properties.containerTitle: CSL's container-title — the journal, book or site the work appears in — stored in camel case because the Cypher dialect has no quoted identifiers; container-title itself cannot be written
properties.fetched: what answered the record, when, and from which identifier
properties.file: the work's own file, a PDF, as the core's blob reference with its mediaType
properties.id: the work's identity, a UUID the shell mints; the node id is node:<id>
properties.kind: the CSL type of the work: article-journal, book, chapter, paper-conference, thesis, report, webpage, post, dataset, software or document
properties.publisherPlace: CSL's publisher-place, stored in camel case for the same reason
properties.title: the work's title

content.semantics: A work as the instance's bibliography held it before BO_0313 — a root node with its record in CSL-JSON shape — read only by bibliography's migration-bo-0313-sources-are-documents, which makes each a document carrying record: source and the built-in Source, rewrites every citation to name it and retires the work. Nothing writes one any more: a source is a document (BO_0313_Q1). The record's two hyphenated CSL keys were stored as containerTitle and publisherPlace. The declaration stays one release, so an install that has not yet run the migration reads its works, and is dropped by the next (BO_0313_026).

content.rationale: BO_0313_Q1: every work becomes a source document and every citation is rewritten to name it, automatically as the release is taken (BO_0312_Q7). The route answers one script: each established work becomes a document with its title and record: source, an empty paragraph for the person's notes, Source taken and its fields filled from the record, its file moved to File; every cite run of an established text block naming a work is rewritten to name the new document, its locator kept, so every reference list reads as before; and each work is retired. An instance without works answers an empty statement. The work declaration stays one release, so an install that has not yet run this reads its works, and is dropped by the next (BO_0313_026).

conventions.citeByRun: A citation is a run of the sentence carrying cite: {work: <workId>, locator?} and empty text, proposed with propose_document_changes like any change to the sentence; workId is the source document's identity as read_works answers it. Never write the number: the document's read derives it.
conventions.fetchDontDraft: A source that is not here is fetched with fetch_record — its DOI, ISBN, PMID, arXiv id or an address — and proposed with propose_work. Never draft a record from memory: a wrong author or year in a reference is worse than no reference. An interview, a conversation or anything with no identifier is the person's to add.
conventions.locatorWhenItHelps: Give a locator — p. 12, §3, fig. 2 — when the claim rests on one place in a long work; leave it out otherwise.
conventions.oneWorkOnce: propose_work refuses a source already here and names it: cite that one.
conventions.readBeforeCiting: Read the sources with read_works before citing, and cite by the workId it answers. A source cited twice keeps its number.
conventions.sourcesAreDocuments: A source is a document using the Source structure, of any CSL type — a paper, a book, a web page, an interview, a conversation, a dataset, software, a report. Its body holds the person's notes on it: read it with read_document when what you cite rests on them.

content.goal: Cite what a claim rests on, from the sources here, where a reader would want to follow it; add a source only from a record you fetched.
content.outputContract: A conclusion naming the sources you cited and any you proposed; zero or more sources staged into the run's group; the sentences carrying their cite runs staged beside them.
content.permittedOperations: read_works to read the sources; fetch_record, the kernel's, to fetch a record; propose_work to stage a source into your group; propose_document_changes to stage a sentence carrying a cite run. Nothing you hold writes truth.
preconditions: The bibliography extension is active: read_works answers. If it does not, say so and cite nothing.
You can say which sentence the source supports; a citation stands where a claim does.

content.description: Propose a source: the record fetch_record answered for it, as it came — one CSL-JSON item of any type, a paper, a web page, an interview, a dataset — and what you fetched it from. The source is staged into your proposal group as a document using the Source structure, its fields filled from the record, never written as truth: the person accepts it with the rest. A source sharing a DOI, an ISBN or an address with one already here is refused, naming that source: cite it instead. Fetch the record first; do not draft one from memory. Once proposed, cite it by the workId this answers, which is the source document's identity.

from.description: the identifier or address you fetched it from

record.description: one CSL-JSON item as fetch_record answered it

content.description: The sources at your pin — every document using the Source structure, of any kind: each one's identity as workId, a line saying who, when and what, its record but for the abstract, and whether it holds a file, narrowed by every word of an optional query. Read it before citing: a citation names a source by the workId this answers. It stages nothing.

query.description: words to narrow by: an author, a title word, a year, a DOI, a tag

content.name: read_works

conventions.atomicProposal: One extension change is one proposal group: every staged revision and relation belongs to the same group and is accepted or rejected as a unit. Never trickle per-file proposals; a half-applied extension state must never be materializable.
conventions.consolidate: Working mode consolidate: narrow the field. Name what now seems durable, merge duplicates by refining the proposal that stands (refines) rather than adding beside it, withdraw weaker or surplus framings with a successor (withdraw), state the consequences of what is kept, and prepare the decision the person takes. Close at least as much as you open: a consolidating run that adds more new blocks than it withdraws or refines is judged as having strayed. (BO_0306)
conventions.create: Working mode create: write. Stage in small reviewable units — one proposal per coherent change, each answerable on its own — and make the assumptions each rests on visible in its note or its words, so the person can accept, reject or refine one without taking the whole drift of the run. (BO_0306)
conventions.deepen: Pinch in (the run's instructions name it when a person zoomed in on a block): the person asked for the next useful layer of that block, and wrote no words. Search the web for news on the block's subject with the search tool, and cite what you use. Deepen at the same level of intent: examples, edge cases, mechanisms, trade-offs, or why it matters. Propose one rewrite of the block that leaves it clear and complete: finish a fragmentary thought keeping its direction, restate what is vague, split mixed ideas, and name the implied assumption. Propose new blocks below it for what the search and the deepening found, each its own item. Propose no gather and no move. (BO_0322)
conventions.explore: Working mode explore (the run's instructions name it when the person chose it): widen the field. Surface alternatives rather than one answer, preserve ambiguity the material has not settled, ask the sharper question, and keep each candidate cheap to discard — say in its note that it is a candidate. Present nothing as settled: no status change, and settled words are left standing rather than rewritten. Adding several proposals is proportionate here. (BO_0306)
conventions.gather: Pinch out (the run's instructions name it when a person zoomed out on a block): the person asked for more structure, and wrote no words. Read the block's neighbours outward in both directions, one at a time, and stop in a direction at the first that does not belong with it. Propose exactly one item of kind gather, and nothing else, since a gather stands alone in its proposal: the block, the unbroken stretch you took in document order with the block among them, and the summary as runs. The summary is a short form, such as a title, claim, takeaway, decision, todo or one-line gist, covering the block, what it gathers and the focused work it already has. When no neighbour fits, stage nothing and say so. (BO_0322)
conventions.humanWritesCostAConfirmation: Every human-class write from the shell parks at the kernel bridge and waits for a confirmation on the kernel's own origin — no human mutation travels from the app origin to CCGW. Budget one cross-origin confirmation per write. That is proportionate for occasional truth like creating a channel and disproportionate for continuous editing, so a surface that writes on every keystroke needs a different shape than one that writes on a button.
conventions.oneOpenProposalPerBlock: A block carries at most one open proposal: every block type declares singleOpenCandidate, so a candidate of a block another open group already holds a candidate of is refused by the core — there is no second candidate to stage beside the first. Work bearing on such a block builds on the candidate that stands, staged into that group as a refinement (the document tools' refines; conventions.openProposals of ui.shell.documents), rather than opening a competing one, so the person answers once. Nothing here answers a proposal: accepting and rejecting stay the person's (proofsAreNotProposals). (BO_0271)
conventions.proofsAreNotProposals: Never stage a proposal whose intended outcome is rejection. A proof-only group is indistinguishable from a real one at the review surface — the rationale is rendered as ordinary text — so after a run of proposals that all deserved acceptance, one that did not will be accepted by the same motion. Construct demonstrations so the refusal is the whole proof and stop there: a refused mutation stages nothing and opens no group. Acceptance is the one non-delegable human action in the architecture and its entire value is the attention behind it, so anything that produces frequent near-identical almost-always-correct proposals is spending that attention down.
conventions.reportWhatStaged: Your closing words report only what this run staged. Name each thing as proposed — a proposal the person accepts or rejects — never as done, created or changed before they accept it. Before you write that you made, changed or removed something, check that a tool call in this run answered success for it. When the command asks for something no tool you hold can do, or a tool refused it, say so plainly: name that part of the command and the refusal's words, and do not describe it as done or imply it will appear. A command carried out in part names what was staged and what was not. Staging nothing is a legitimate outcome and is said as such (the output contract). (BO_0343)
conventions.understand: Working mode understand: read more than you write. Trace definitions and dependencies, tell established material from open proposals, and answer with a map of what follows from what — relations with their reasons, and short explanatory blocks placed where the command asks. Leave the document's own blocks alone unless the command referenced them: rewriting, removing or moving an unreferenced established block is judged as having strayed. (BO_0306)
conventions.valuesTravelAsParameters:
How a statement says values, which the grammar will not let you guess:
- Every value beyond a scalar travels beside the statement in the tool call's parameters field, which is one JSON object written as text — for example parameters: "{\"bid\": \"art-x.b1\", \"runs\": [{\"text\": \"...\"}]}". The statement writes $name where a value belongs; lists and objects have no literal form inside the statement itself, and runs: [{text: ...}] inline is a parse error every time.
- Every $name in the statement must have a key in that JSON object. An empty parameters value beside a parameterized statement is always wrong, and resending a refused statement without filling it changes nothing.
- A script is one or more statements separated by semicolons; CREATE ... RELATE ... in one breath is a parse error at RELATE. Aliases scope per statement but parameters are request-global, so one parameters object serves the whole script: the canonical block write is CREATE (n:Text {id: $bid, runs: $runs, order: $order}); RELATE childRef -[r:CONTAINS]-> parentRef, with bid, runs, order, childRef and parentRef all keys of the one JSON object.
- RELATE endpoint refs resolve from parameters — <ref>NodeId first, then <ref> — and those values carry the node: prefix (childRef: "node:art-x.b1"), even though the id property inside CREATE content is bare. The ref names an existing node; the id property mints one.
- When syntax is uncertain, calliopa_explain compiles a statement without executing it. Explain and correct rather than retrying a refusal unchanged — the diagnostics name what they want.
conventions.whereRequirementsLive: An extension's requirements and open work live in its own docs/ members (docs/system/**/*.md under the live-line protocol), read through calliopa_query like its code. An extension's changes are its own docs/changes/ members (BO_0254): docs/changes/<PREFIX>_NNNN_TYPE_<short-name>.md in its subtree, finished ones under docs/changes/completed/, each carrying its status in a Status: line from idea, draft, ready, wip, completed, rejected. They are written and revised the way every other docs member is — from a checkout, in the proposal that carries the code — and rendered read-only in the shell's Extensions section. A run working from the composer holds no checkout and so writes none. A run that changes an extension's behaviour also updates its docs in the same proposal group and keeps its change document's Status: line honest — wip when it claims ready work, completed when the work is done; only a person establishes draft or ready, and acceptance is what establishes any status. (BO_0201, BO_0254)
conventions.workVocabulary: Documents carry reason-bearing relations between blocks (BO_0244). Two rules, whichever tool writes them: a relation is proposed with a reason naming the condition that connects its ends — never that they seem related — and with origin inferred or derived, since a run never declares; and each end names a block by blockId, of this document or another, never a retired or discarded one, and never the same block twice. Propose these through propose_document_changes (items relate, reason), never by statement, so review sees them as the editor would have written them. (BO_0288, BO_0324)
conventions.writeShapeFollowsFrequency: Choose the write path by how often the operation happens, not by what it touches. Continuous editing stages candidates with no confirmation and one deliberate act to establish them; an occasional deliberate act — creating a channel, filing something into one — takes the confirmation directly, where the ceremony is proportionate. Both are the same architecture; only the frequency differs, and reaching for one shape everywhere makes typing intolerable or truth too cheap.

content.goal: Stage work into Calliopa's graph as one reviewable proposal, whatever the reader's intention was.
content.outputContract: Zero or one open proposal group. Zero is a legitimate outcome and must be said plainly rather than filled with a placeholder.
preconditions: The run is bound to one proposal group at a pinned dataRevision; nothing staged becomes truth without human acceptance.
The intention's own skill, if the run has one, carries what to produce; this one carries how any of it is staged.

content.completionRule: An accepted proposal group: the run stages one atomic change, a human accepts it, and the activity is over.
content.label: Extend

conventions.authoringRoutes: Two routes produce the same graph shape; pick one per change and never mix them. (1) Direct CCGW staging — what the examples below show: you write CREATE/SET and stage every partOf and dependsOn relation yourself. (2) The materializer round-trip — checkout into a working tree, edit files, commit — which derives partOf from the tree layout and dependsOn from the manifest dependencies map, so you never write a relation by hand. Route 2 is the default for human and agent authoring alike, and the kernel workspace tools ARE route 2 for a run: calliopa_workspace_checkout, _list, _read, _edit, _create, _delete, _build, _check, _test, _diff and _commit work a real tree on the kernel and stage its whole diff into your group. A Block that does not materialize (ext.skill, ext.settings, ext.migration, ext.blocktype, ext.relationtype, ext.intention) is reached by route 1, or carried by a members sidecar on kernel commit --members.
conventions.binaryAssets: Binary files travel: a binary in the diff becomes an ext.source Block whose code is a blob reference, the bytes uploaded through PUT /v1/blobs before the referencing mutation and hash-verified. The shell's favicon, PNGs and font ship this way.
conventions.breakingChanges: Tightening an established definition is gated; loosening it is free. Adding a required property, adding a unique property already duplicated, narrowing permitted children, enabling singleOpenCandidate, renaming, or removing a definition are breaking *when the type has established content* — and only then, so the same change is refused on a populated type and permitted on an empty one. A breaking change needs an ext.migration Block in the same group naming the types it covers, with a rationale and the operations that transform existing content travelling alongside; its authority is the human review of that group, not machinery. Removing a required property needs none, because requiring less invalidates nothing.
conventions.capabilities: The manifest capabilities object carries renders — the surface kinds the extension renders, as plural nouns: routes, views — and ccgwScopes, the CCGW operations its skills need, absent when the extension reads nothing. Nothing validates the shape, so a misspelled capabilities key builds clean and is never noticed.
conventions.checkWhereEnforcementRuns: A declaration is only enforced where something reads it. permittedChildTypes is honoured by the pages layer, and the pages layer is mounted in the production cell rather than the dogfood app — so in a dogfood deployment the declaration is real, resolved, and unenforced. Before relying on any declared constraint, find the code that acts on it and confirm that code is reachable from where the writes happen. When it is not, the surface owns the constraint and the gap belongs in the record.
conventions.codeRun: A run that changes an extension names the change document it works on, and everything follows from that: the run stages into that change's own proposal group rather than one minted for the run, so however many runs a change takes it arrives as ONE proposal for the person to answer; and the build tree belongs to that group, so a second run finds the first's tree with its dependencies already installed. The order: read the extension's docs/ and the change document the run names — the requirements live there, not in the command; calliopa_workspace_checkout; read and edit with the workspace tools; then calliopa_workspace_build, calliopa_workspace_check and calliopa_workspace_test until all three are green, because the person does not read your diff and the green gates plus your own account of what you did are most of what they judge the change by; then calliopa_workspace_commit with a rationale. Write the docs and the change document's Status: line in the SAME commit as the code: a proposal that changes behaviour and leaves the docs behind is incomplete and is not accepted as complete.
conventions.crossExtensionImports: The shell imports its extensions and an extension may import the shell's lib and server modules by the ~/ alias; the tree is one pnpm package, so every import resolves and builds. Nothing enforces the manifest's dependsOn against those imports — declare what you import anyway, because the dependency edge is what makes the relationship traversable in the graph.
conventions.declaredBaseline: On the direct CCGW route the mutation must carry dataRevision — the pin the change was computed against. An auto-created proposal group records it as its baseDataRevision, and acceptance conflict-checks against that base. Omit it and the group bases at 0, so acceptance refuses with mutation_resolution_failed conflicts with truth that moved past its base revision 0 — a refusal that names a conflict but is really a missing baseline, and that only appears at acceptance, long after staging looked successful. The materializer route passes the checkout pin for you, which is why this trap belongs to route 1 alone.
conventions.definitionShape: Definition fields are data, not prose. In an ext.blocktype or ext.relationtype Block, requiredProperties, uniqueProperties, permittedChildTypes and runProperties are lists of property-name strings; block and singleOpenCandidate are booleans. A string where a list belongs parses to nothing at all — uniqueProperties: "name among active channels" declares no unique property and the rule silently never fires, which is far worse than a refusal because the definition still reads correctly to a human. Put the qualifier in a separate descriptive field, never inside the declaration. The same rule governs the manifest: dependencies is a map of extension id to semver range, capabilities is an object, and category is exactly bundled or individual.
conventions.dependencyReferences: A dependency on another extension is a dependsOn relation from the depending manifest to the dependency manifest, with the semver range recorded in the depending manifest dependencies map keyed by extension id — the range is content because a relation stores no properties, and the relation is what makes the dependency traversable. On the materializer route kernel commit derives the edge from the map; on the direct route you stage it. A dependencies entry naming an extension with no manifest, established or added by the same change, is refused. Two extensions added together may depend on each other. The range is checked twice: the registry scan fails a build whose tree holds a version outside a declared range (dependency_out_of_range), and the kernel refuses a version flip or an activation that would serve one before writing it (BO_0219). A version is the manifest version label at the subtree's last established state under it: bump version when you want a state of the subtree to be a version a person can serve from the extension view; two revisions under one label are one version, its last state.
conventions.deploymentIsSeparate: Acceptance and deployment are two acts. Accepting a proposal establishes truth at a new dataRevision; the kernel keeps serving the promoted release pin until kernel pin --to head moves it, building the candidate before it promotes. An accepted extension is therefore not yet a running one, and nothing warns that the two have diverged — verify the surface appears rather than inferring it from acceptance.
conventions.derivedFiles: Files matching *.gen.* are build output, never content, and the commit path skips them. The tree root's node_modules/, dist/ and server/ are the build's derived directories and are never committed either; a nested src/server/ is ordinary source.
conventions.docs: An extension carries its owner's knowledge beside its code, as ext.source members under docs/: docs/system/<area>/<topic>.md under the live-line protocol — a list item's marker is its commitment (* fixed, - mutable), its checkbox its state ([ ] open, [x] claimed, none is truth), a line beginning 'Functional question' awaits the owner, and a task identifier (XX_0000_000) ties a line to the change that made it true. docs/system/system.md's Purpose section is what the extension is for; README.md is the fallback; the skill's goal is the last resort. An extension's changes are its own docs/changes/ members (BO_0254): docs/changes/<PREFIX>_NNNN_TYPE_<short-name>.md in its subtree, finished ones under docs/changes/completed/, each carrying its status in a Status: line from idea, draft, ready, wip, completed, rejected. They are written and revised the way every other docs member is — from a checkout, in the proposal that carries the code — and rendered read-only in the shell's Extensions section. A run working from a checkout writes them like any other member, in the proposal that carries the code — which is what the workspace tools are for. BO_0254 decided that a change document is not written through the DOCUMENT tools (create_document carries neither change nor status), not that a run holds no checkout. The shell renders the system docs as a navigable network for the owner, so a change to an extension is not complete until its docs say so: convert the [x] lines you claimed into truth, add [ ] follow-ups for what remains, keep the identifiers, and write the change document's Status: line in the same proposal. Read the docs before changing the code; they are where the requirements live. (BO_0201, BO_0254) An extension may be started from the shell's Extensions section with a manifest and a docs/system/system.md alone — its purpose under Purpose, version 0.1.0, individual, no entrypoint, nothing to serve (BO_0224); the first topic names the extension's prefix, and the first code arrives through this skill as a proposal. An extension can leave an instance as one file — the kernel's export: its tree — its change documents among it — and its members — and enter another as a proposal the owner accepts, arriving switched off; ext.settings, activation and pins never travel, and the archive's category lands as individual.
conventions.domainVocabulary: A domain vocabulary is ext.blocktype and ext.relationtype Blocks in an extension of its own, depending on ui.shell — never inside the shell, which stays domain-neutral. Neither Block materializes, so the definitions are staged through direct CCGW or a members sidecar while the extension's sources go through the materializer; that is one rung, two routes, and they must not be mixed inside a single change. Declare uniqueness with uniqueProperties and let the lifecycle carry the qualifier: declared uniqueness is scoped to established revisions, so retiring a node frees its unique values and a "retired" or "archived" flag kept in content does not, because a flagged node stays established and keeps claiming them.
conventions.draftingSurfacesReadThroughTheirDraft: A surface that stages before establishing has two halves, and the staged half is invisible by design. Staged content is a candidate and does not resolve at head, so every read in a drafting surface must carry the draft’s overlay — the list that finds unoffered drafts, and the read that shows what was just written. Getting this wrong does not produce an error: it produces a dead end, where the author is told to offer a draft they cannot see or reach. Verify that the author can see what they wrote, not only that the write succeeded.
conventions.featureExtensions: A feature extension carries code, not values. The first is settings: src/extensions/settings/ holds the view (settings.tsx), the server modules (server/connections.ts, server/connection-tests.ts, server/adapters.ts) and the feature's migrations (migrations/*.sql, one sequence with the shell's own migrations/ ordered by file name and applied by the tree's serve entry). The shell keeps the thin route files under src/routes/api/settings/ importing from ~/extensions/settings/server/…, and its manifest declares dependencies {"ui.shell": ">=0.1.0"}. Values the feature stores stay where the feature keeps them — the shell's encrypted connection store — never in ext.settings Blocks, which are plain graph content.
conventions.freshNamesAreForced: A graph definition may never shadow a code-registered type, so the frozen vocabulary’s names are unavailable: Page, Paragraph, Note and Document are all taken. Reincarnating a model therefore means fresh names carrying proven mechanics — which is the intended posture anyway, but the refusal enforces it whether or not you meant it.
conventions.migrations: The tree owns its schema. scripts/lib/migrations.mjs reads migrations/ and every src/extensions/<id>/migrations/ as one sequence ordered by file name, records each in schema_migrations, and the serve entry applies pending ones before it listens — except under the promotion gate's probe (CALLIOPA_SERVE_PROBE=1), which never migrates. Number a new migration after the highest existing one across both places.
conventions.naming: The manifest id is the extension id — lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, in parts joined by a dot or a hyphen, exactly ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([.-][a-z0-9]+)*$, the rule the kernel's create enforces (BO_0224) — and must equal its directory name under src/extensions/ — the commit path refuses a mismatch. Source Blocks are <extId>.<path>. A contribution Block, if one is ever staged, carries a content id equal to its file name.
conventions.orderingLivesOnTheChild: Ordering is a content property on the child block, never on the containment relation, because a Relation stores no properties — a core-model fact, not a design choice. Use a base-36 fractional string compared as an ordinary string, so inserting between two siblings mints a key between theirs and writes one block instead of renumbering the set.
conventions.rulesTheGraphCannotExpress: Some settled rules have no home in the meta-schema and end up enforced in surfaces: which node types are ineligible as a relation’s endpoints, and permitted children wherever the enforcing layer is unreachable. Record each one where the rule is written rather than letting the surface be its only statement, because a rule living only in a surface is a rule the next surface will not know.
conventions.shellShape: The shell of this graph is calliopa-app, imported as ui.shell (BO_0200): a Qwik City application with file-convention routes under src/routes/ and compiled-in views (src/lib/views.ts), root-mapped as a whole. There is no runtime registry, no generated route map and no ext.uicontribution contract in this shell — the kernel still validates contribution Blocks on commit, but nothing reads them. An extension reaches the user through the shell's own source: the shell imports the extension's modules by path (~/extensions/<extId>/…) from a route file under src/routes/, a view entry in src/lib/views.ts, or a server module — so a new feature extension is one proposal that adds the subtree and the import lines in the shell, both root-mapped by the same kernel commit.
conventions.structuralVocabularies: A vocabulary with structure — containment, ordering, permitted children — is a different problem from a vocabulary of flat types. Reuse the code-registered CONTAINS relation rather than declaring a fresh containment type: the block machinery that enforces permitted children and nesting bounds resolves block types through the effective schema, so fresh graph-defined types inherit it, but every containment operation is written against CONTAINS. A fresh containment relation leaves permittedChildTypes declared and inert, which is the silent-no-op failure this system works hardest to avoid.
conventions.subtreeShape: One ext.manifest Block is the subtree root. Every member Block — ext.source, ext.blocktype, ext.relationtype, ext.skill, ext.uicontribution — carries a partOf relation to that manifest.
conventions.uiContributionContract: Retired with the calliopa-app shell. ext.uicontribution Blocks are still a valid member kind the kernel validates on commit (kind route, panel or command; content id equal to the file name), but this shell reads none of them; declare UI through the shell's own imports instead (shellShape).
conventions.wholeTreeCommits: The materializer diff is whole-tree: kernel commit stages everything that differs from the lockfile, not the subtree you were working in. Running the repository's own formatter while authoring an extension can therefore rewrite another extension's sources and stage them alongside your work — observed rewriting className to class across ui.shell. Check kernel status before every commit and confirm the file list is only yours; a foreign file in the list is a signal to stop, not a detail to accept.

content.goal: Create a new extension, or evolve an existing one, as a complete subtree of Blocks staged in exactly one atomic proposal through CCGW.
content.outputContract: Exactly one open proposal group staging the complete extension change — manifest, member Blocks, their partOf relations, and any dependsOn relations — with rationale and provenance. No writes outside the proposal, no established status, no partial subtree that could materialize half-applied. On the materializer route the same group is produced by kernel commit, with partOf and dependsOn derived rather than written by hand; the resulting graph shape is identical.
preconditions: The extension meta-schema definition Blocks are established truth; read the ext.blocktype and ext.relationtype definitions before staging.
The target extension id is decided and does not collide with an existing ext.manifest id.
Every extension named in the manifest dependencies map has a manifest, established or added by this same change.
The mutation context declares an agent identity scoped to one open proposal group; a skill execution never writes established truth.

content.rationale: BO_0272 narrows text.disposition from keep, pin, resolved, discarded, prompt to fixate, discarded, prompt: the standing scale becomes three states — discard, keep, fixate — where keep is the absence of a value (user decision, 2026-09-21). Nothing is lost. A block carrying pin reads as fixate, which is the same standing under its own name; one carrying resolved reads as discarded, the remaining state for a block its reader had set aside; one carrying the old keep reads as the resting state, which is what the word now means. The mapping is the kernel's StandingOf and the shell's RETIRED, so a reader and a run are told the same of one block, and the next write stores the new value. This instance carried no block with any disposition when the declaration was revised (90 text blocks, checked over CCGW on 2026-09-21), so no content operation travels with it here.

BO_0315 narrows text.disposition from fixate, discarded, prompt to fixate, prompt: the standing scale becomes keep and fixate, and a block the reader removes is retired rather than discarded (user decision, 2026-09-30). Nothing is lost. The route answers one script that retires every text block stored as discarded or resolved, keeping its place — the value cleared, the containment closed and the block related retired from its document, as the bar's retirement does — so each can be restored from Show removed like any retired block. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003), on this instance and on every install that takes the release.

BO_0324 removes calliopa-refine, calliopa-show, calliopa-video and test with their data, and what existed only for refinement: block kinds, claims, judgements, derived blocks and the root's phase (BO_0324_Q1, BO_0324_Q2, BO_0324_Q5). The relations stored against claims are deleted with them (BO_0324_Q6). The route answers one script that clears kind on every text block, a document's phase, supersededBy and acceptedAt, and an intention of refine; closes every relation on a claim, a judgement or a relation anchored on a claim, every derivedFrom edge and an investigation's focuses edge; and retires those nodes and the documents recorded as investigations. A type no longer declared reads as empty, so the route answers nothing on a graph that never held refinement or that it has already run on. Relations of asserts, judges and derivedFrom that an earlier write left active on nodes it retired stand on retired ends and are read by nothing; they stay in the store's history, and this member's revision, staged with the declarations' removal, is what covers their types leaving.

BO_0336 moves what a picture or a video is made with from the profile to a format: the document declaration drops profileType and imageBackend in the same release. The route answers one script clearing both from every established document holding either, and nothing when none does. Nothing moves to a format: a profile names a format by the person's choice (user decision, 2026-10-02). The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

content.name: focuses
content.semantics: A document is focused work on a block: directed from the child document to the text block it elaborates, at most one document per block, the shell's rule. The block keeps its place in its parent; deleting the child closes the edge. Declared by ui.shell under CA_0047_001.

content.name: retired
content.semantics: Records that a block left a document's reading order without being deleted, directed from the document to the block. Retiring a block closes its CONTAINS validity and creates this relation in the same mutation; restoring closes this relation and creates a new CONTAINS. Closing containment alone would strand the block beyond any rooted read, so retirement is recorded as its own relation and the retired list is an ordinary read from the document. Containment itself is the core's CONTAINS relation and needs no declaration here.

conventions.changeDocuments: An extension's changes are its own docs/changes/ members (BO_0254): docs/changes/<PREFIX>_NNNN_TYPE_<short-name>.md in its subtree, finished ones under docs/changes/completed/, each carrying its status in a Status: line from idea, draft, ready, wip, completed, rejected. They are written and revised the way every other docs member is — from a checkout, in the proposal that carries the code — and rendered read-only in the shell's Extensions section. A run working from the composer holds no checkout and so writes none. A document tool never writes one: create_document takes a title and a first block and nothing else. (BO_0254)
conventions.marks: A run carries text and, when it has any, marks among bold, italic, strikethrough and code, and may carry a link. Marks are not declared in the graph's vocabulary; the editor's set is the one that renders.
conventions.notes: A read and each proposed item may carry a note: one short line, at most 80 characters, saying what you do with the block. The person sees it on the block while you work, and on the proposal after. Give one when the plain words — Reading, Proposes a rewrite, Proposes removal — would not say what you are doing; leave it out otherwise. A note is never the change itself (BO_0265).
conventions.openProposals: The document you work in is not settled: other runs' proposals may stand unanswered on its blocks, and read_document answers them (BO_0271). Every block carries proposal — {group, item, proposer, kind, words, refinable, reason} — when another group has proposed against it, and the document carries proposedInserts, the new blocks proposed into it, each with where it would stand. Read them before writing anything new. What stands and needs sharpening is refined in place, never proposed again beside it: a block keeps one open proposal, so a second rewrite of the same block is refused by the core. A refinement is a replace carrying refines: {group, item} — the group and item read_document answered — with the runs and, if it changes, the role; it lands on that proposal's candidate, under that group, and the person answers once. A proposed insert is refined the same way, by its group and item. Stage only what needs changing. Where a standing proposal already says what you would say, leave its words as they are; say that you left it plainly only when there is really nothing to add anywhere. The document's own blocks — accepted text — are left as they are unless the command referenced one (a marked block or passage) or plainly asks for those words to change; every proposal the person has not answered is open matter, accepted words are not. A proposal whose refinable is false is context: read it, build on what it says, never propose against it — its reason says why: a run still going may restage the same block a moment later, another person's branch is theirs, a fixated framing is kept, an answered member is settled, and a removal or a move has no words to refine. Your final words say what you refined and whose it was, and what you left standing because it already said it. When the command asks to reconcile, merge or reduce the standing proposals (BO_0286): refine the proposals that stay, so the reconciled words live in them; withdraw the ones those words make surplus with a withdraw item — proposal: {group, item}, successor: the standing item or the index of the item in this call that supersedes it, withdrawalReason: one short line where the successor does not say it — and stage nothing beside them. A withdrawal is a proposal, never an answer: the item stays open with its words, the person rejects it with one press or accepts it anyway, and accepting the successor rejects what it supersedes in the same press. Any withdrawable item may be withdrawn, a removal or a move too, which then leaves the block as it stands. The final words say how many proposals were refined and how many withdrawn, and in whose favour.
conventions.prompts: A block with the prompt standing is a command the reader wrote in the document and sent, not material of it (BO_0267): never rewrite, remove or move it, and do not build on it unless the command asks. When your run was sent from a block, the instructions name it. Every command given in a document is answered by proposing into it: when the command asks a question, the answer is staged directly after the block the command was sent from, as the blocks the reader should read it as (conventions.structure), and your final words say what you staged.
conventions.readerAnswersPerItem: Each item is decided on its own in the editor. Keep an item to one intent, so a reader can accept the heading and reject the rewrite.
conventions.relations: Reason-bearing relations connect blocks: a relate item names its source and its target by blockId, of this document or another, never a retired or discarded block and never the same block twice. A relation is proposed with a reason naming the condition that connects its ends (cache reuse is safe only while the context is unchanged), never that they seem related, and with origin inferred or derived — a run never declares. A relation ends by its state and is never removed. (BO_0244, BO_0288, BO_0324)
conventions.structure: What you stage arrives as the structure you wrote, never as one block holding all of it (BO_0270). Split the content at its headings: a heading is its own text block with the role it has — h1, h2, h3 — and a block's runs never carry # characters, which nothing renders. Under a heading each paragraph is its own block, and each list item is its own block with its marker as plain text, since no role renders a list; a fenced code block stays one text block, because it is one unit; and a table is a table block — kind table, with its typed columns (text, number, date, boolean) and its rows, one block whole (BO_0287) — never pipes in a paragraph. An equation is an equation block — kind equation, carrying the exact TeX it is set from, optionally a caption and numbered when its author asks for a number (BO_0290) — never TeX in a paragraph; mathematics inside a sentence is a run of that sentence carrying math: true whose text is its TeX, and a reference to a numbered equation is a run carrying equationRef with that equation's identity and no text of its own. A picture carries an optional caption and numbered when its author asks for a figure number, and a table numbered likewise (BO_0295); A code block carries an optional caption and numbered when its author asks for a listing number, counted apart from figures and tables (BO_0303); read_document answers a numbered code block's number, and a reference to it reads Listing N; a reference to a numbered figure — a picture, or an output a person numbered — is a run carrying figureRef with its identity and no text of its own, and to a numbered table a run carrying tableRef. A reference to any block of the document — a section by its heading, a paragraph, or a numbered figure, table or equation — is a run of its sentence carrying blockRef with that block's identity and no text of its own (BO_0300); read_document answers each as its label — Figure 3, Table 1, (2), the heading's words, or Remark N for a paragraph another sentence refers to, which the manuscript then sets apart as a numbered remark — or missing when the block is outside the reading order; prefer blockRef over figureRef, tableRef and equationRef, which remain read for the sentences that carry them. A citation is a run of its sentence carrying cite — {work, locator?}: the identity of a work of the instance's bibliography, and where in it when the claim rests on one place, such as p. 12 — whose text is empty, never a bracketed number or an author and year typed into the words (BO_0291); read_document answers each citation's number, or missing when its work is gone, and how the reader sees it drawn is the document's citation style. Never set a caption or numbered on an output: an output is what an execution produced, and its caption and number are the person's. A number is never written: read_document answers the number the document's order gives each numbered equation, figure, table and listing — each kind counted apart — and a reference answers the number it resolves to, or missing when its block is gone or asks for none. A change to a table is a replace of that one block carrying the whole table; where a file stands behind it, read_document says so with its row count and the rows you read are its first hundred, and your replace drops the file, since the cells you propose are the whole table. A paper's abstract is one text block with the role abstract, wherever it stands; a manuscript's authors, affiliations, keywords and venue are the document's own properties, set by a person, and a run proposes none of them (BO_0293). Never invent structure: content that carries no heading is given none, and a one-sentence answer is one block by this rule rather than by an exception. A rewrite carries it too: rewriting a block into content with headings stages the replace beside the inserts in the one group, with the rationale saying the items are one change.

content.goal: Read and propose changes to the documents a reader writes in, through the kernel toolset's document tools, so a run's proposal lands exactly what the editor would have written and is reviewed per item.
content.outputContract: One propose_document_changes call per coherent change to one document, with a rationale saying why. Report the group the tool answered and what it stages; never claim the change is accepted. A refusal envelope is an answer: read its diagnostics and adjust the items rather than retrying the same call. A refinement is reported as what it refined and whose proposal that was; a standing proposal left as it stands because it already says it is reported as left, not as done (conventions.openProposals). A reconciliation is reported as how many standing proposals were refined and how many withdrawn, and in whose favour, never as new blocks staged beside them.
content.permittedOperations: list_documents to find a document by title, and an extension's changes by change — each row carries change and status for a change document; read_document for its blocks in reading order with their identities, kinds, roles and runs, and for a change document its extension and status; read_blocks for only the blocks it names, in reading order and in read_document's shape, which is how the person sees what you look at (BO_0265); propose_document_changes with items of kind replace (runs and/or role for a block), insert (a new text or divider block at a placement), remove (a block leaves the reading order, retired rather than deleted), move (a block to a placement) and status (a change document's status, one of idea, draft, ready, wip, completed, rejected); create_document for a new document with a title, its first block and — for a change of an extension — change naming the extension and a status, idea unless said. Everything stages into this run's proposal group; nothing writes truth. The statement tools remain available for anything beyond documents. — and, since BO_0244, relate (a reason-bearing relation between two blocks) and reason (a relation's new reason). read_document answers each block's provenance and the document's relations with both ends. Since BO_0271, read_document and read_blocks answer on each block its proposal — the standing proposal another group holds against it: group, item, proposer, kind (rewrite, removal, move), words, refinable and, when not refinable, reason — and the document's proposedInserts, each with its placement; and a replace item may carry refines: {group, item}, landing its runs and role on that proposal's candidate in that group instead of in this run's, which is how a standing proposal is refined (conventions.openProposals). Since BO_0286, withdraw: {kind: "withdraw", proposal: {group, item}, successor?: {group, item} | {index}, withdrawalReason?} marks a standing proposal as surplus, on the proposal itself, for the person to reject with one press; read_document answers each standing proposal's withdrawable and, when a run has proposed one, its withdrawnBy — the run, its agent, the successor and the reason (conventions.openProposals).
content.preconditions: The run holds the kernel toolset. The document to change exists at the run's pin; read it once with read_document to find your way, then read the blocks you work on with read_blocks before proposing against them — the person sees each block you read marked while you read it — because a replace or a move names a block by the identity those reads answered.

content.rationale: BO_0311 chooses the profile per command in the chip, and makes Profile a built-in role every profile carries (BO_0308_Q5, BO_0308_Q7, BO_0311_Q1). The route answers one script relating every document carrying record profile that does not take builtin:profile to it, and clearing the profile slot every document still carries from before, so every chip starts at No profile; nothing when both stand. The document declaration drops profile in the same release. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0311_015: a document taking Profile is a profile. A document given Profile from its chip before taking the role wrote record profile carries the role without the record, so the chip, the run start and the grant do not read it as a profile. The route answers one script setting record profile on every such carrier, nothing when all hold it. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0338: profiles are instructions. Every document carrying record profile carries record instruction, and one still titled Untitled profile is titled Untitled instruction, so it stays unnamed. The route answers one script for every such document, nothing once none is left. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0310_Q4: the roles a person chose in the retired Keywords section as the keyword, definition and alias roles merge into the built-ins Keyword, Definition and Alias. The kernel hands the route the extension's settings; it answers one script copying each chosen role's fields (a name the built-in holds kept once, its values rekeyed) and offers onto the built-in, moving every assignment and its roleFields values, and retiring the chosen role, so Roles shows no duplicate and every keyword and mention resolves as before. Nothing chosen, or all merged, answers an empty statement.

conventions.mentionsAreDerived: A mention is resolved from the words when the document is read and stored nowhere: you write the words, and the connection follows. Do not add links, marks or brackets to make one. Where a sentence must name a keyword whose words would not match it, write those words as a run carrying keyword, the keyword document's id, as a person does by typing @; it is words, never a link or an atom.
conventions.neverMark: You never mark a document as a keyword, give it or its blocks a structure, or propose a definition into a keyword's document unless asked to in that document: marking and defining are the person's acts.
conventions.preferTheTitle: Use the keyword's title in your words rather than an alias, so the mention is drawn and the glossary carries the name the person chose. A plural or a possessive of the title is fine; a different word is not the keyword.
conventions.promptKeywordsArrive: The keywords the prompt includes reach you at your start, in their own section of your instructions, with what the person chose to send of each. Write by those words; read_keywords answers the rest of the document.
conventions.readKeywordsFirst: Before proposing into a document, call read_keywords once. Where the document mentions a keyword, its definition is in the answer; where you are about to write a keyword the document does not mention yet, the instance's keywords are listed by name.
conventions.writeByTheDefinition: Write about a keyword as its definition has it. The definition is the person's own account and outranks your idea of the word; where it is silent, the keyword's document is the next place to read.

content.goal: Write about a keyword as the keyword's own document defines it: read the definition before writing, keep the keyword's title, and never mark a document as a keyword yourself.
content.outputContract: A conclusion naming the keywords the proposed words are about and where their definitions were read; the blocks staged into the run's group; no keyword marked and no structure assigned.
content.permittedOperations: read_keywords to read the document's mentions and the instance's keywords; read_document to read a keyword's document whole when its definition is not enough; propose_document_changes to propose the words. Nothing you hold marks a keyword or assigns a structure.
preconditions: read_keywords answers for the document. If the instance holds no keywords, write as you would any document and read nothing more here.
A keyword is a document using the built-in structure Keyword; its definition and its aliases are its blocks using the built-in structures Definition and Alias.

content.description: Called by the kernel at the start of a run a person's command started, never offered to the run (BO_0310_025): the keywords the prompt block includes, named with @ or matched in its words, each with what Keyword's Send with prompt switches on, as one instruction section, and the keywords sent for the record.

content.rationale: BO_0312 makes manuscripts formats. The manuscripts kept before are deleted with the surface that showed them (BO_0312_Q4): the route retires every manuscript node and leaves its blobs to the store's collection. Front matter moves from the document to a role the person owns (BO_0312_Q3): when any document holds authors, affiliations, keywords or a venue, the route creates one ordinary role Paper with the fields Authors and Affiliations (long text, one per line) and Keywords (text), has each such document take it with its values written in, and clears the four properties. The venue was a template id and has no field on Paper; a person's venue role says it now. Paper is an ordinary role afterwards, the person's to rename or change. An instance with nothing to move answers an empty statement. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003), on this instance and on every install that takes the release (BO_0312_Q7).

conventions.aRenditionNotABlock: A rendition is kept on the document carrying Format: it proposes no block and changes no property. Do not describe it as a change to the document.
conventions.nameTheRoles: Name the venue structure and the paper structure your instruction points at. The tool reads their values by field key — template, citationStyle, authors, affiliations, keywords — and answers which it read and which were missing. A missing key is something the person sets on the structure: say so, or propose the value.
conventions.onceIsEnough: Make one rendition, read it, and say what you found. Every rendition is kept on the document and listed with your process; make another only after the document or its structures changed.
conventions.readTheAnswer: The answer is the LaTeX source, the log's warnings, what was left out and the structure fields read and missing — never the PDF. Read the omitted list first: every line names a block the paper could not carry and why. Then the missing fields. Then the warnings. Then the source, for what the venue's rules ask that the document does not give.
conventions.readTheRolesFirst: Read the document's structures before making anything. The document carries Format (PDF), the venue and the paper; the venue and the paper are the person's own structures, named by their ids, never looked up by name. If the document carries no Format, or Format is not a PDF, propose Format on the document rather than calling the tool — never on a block: Format is taken by documents alone. A part to be formatted on its own is opened as a block's focused work, whose document takes Format.
conventions.sayItAsAProposal: What the venue still needs goes into the document as a proposal — the missing block, a question under the section it concerns, a structure value — and into your conclusion. Never edit the source: the manuscript is a projection of the record, and the record is what is corrected.

content.goal: Make a manuscript — a PDF with its LaTeX source and references — of a document using Format, its whole reading order, when an instruction the person wrote tells you to, or when the person asks for one; read what came back and say what the venue still needs as a proposal.
content.outputContract: A conclusion naming the document, the venue, the outcome, which structure fields were read and which were missing, what was left out and what the venue still needs; the kept rendition staged into the run's group with its files; any proposed blocks or structure values staged beside it.
content.permittedOperations: read_document_structures to read the document's structures and their values first. make_manuscript, the kernel's, to make and keep one rendition of the document at your pin, naming the venue structure (its template and citationStyle fields) and the paper structure (its authors, affiliations and keywords) the instruction points at. read_document to read the blocks. propose_document_changes and propose_structures to say what the manuscript needs. Nothing you hold writes truth.
preconditions: The manuscripts extension is active and the instance has a typesetting service: make_manuscript is listed, and refuses in words when there is no service.
The document to make it of uses the built-in Format structure with its type PDF: a manuscript is made of its whole reading order and kept on it. Format is never on a block.
No instruction ships: a fresh install makes no manuscript until the person writes an instruction that asks for one. The instruction's words say which venue and paper structures to name.

conventions.cost: Quote before you generate and say the amount in the vendor's own words. Do not ask for a second confirmation.
conventions.fillTheInputs: Fill each input from the command: the blocks the person marked with # (#1, #2 in the words), matched to the inputs by what the command and the format's words say; the picture above the block when the words point at nothing. Pass them to generate in inputs by name. Say in your answer which picture you used for which input.
conventions.followJob: A running job is not a finished picture or video. Keep collecting its existing job; never start a second job to retry collection.
conventions.formatDecides: The format the instruction names decides what is made and with what — provider, model, ratio and quality — and the variation the person chose beside Send, when there is one. Never name a model, a provider or an option in tool arguments, and never ask the person to choose one in words: a different result needs a variation or another format.
conventions.nameEveryInput: Write the words the vendor is sent yourself, naming every attached input as @name where the words mean it (from @start to @end). generate refuses an attached input the words do not name; it never adds the name for you.
conventions.oneAtATime: Generate at most one image or video in a Send. A second generation requires another Send.
conventions.readTheFormat: Call read_format first. The format's words are instructions for using it: follow them. Its inputs say what it takes, each under a name the words must use as @name.
conventions.theBlockIsThePrompt: Start from the prompt block's words unless the person or task supplies replacement words; add the @names the inputs need.
conventions.videoNeedsAPicture: A video format declaring no input opens on the picture above the block, named @start in the words. Without a picture there, make the picture in an earlier Send under an instruction whose format makes images, then send the words for the motion under one whose format makes video.

content.goal: Generate one image or one video as the format the person's selected instruction names, then leave it in the Send's review group.
content.outputContract: A conclusion naming the generated image or video and its cost status; the pending block and its completed blob staged in the Send's review group.
content.permittedOperations: media.read_format, media.quote_generation, then media.generate once in the Send, then media.collect_generation with the returned pending block and job id until it completes. The kernel admits at most one spending tool call per Send.
preconditions: The Send carries an instruction whose Format field names a format of type image or video. If it names none, tell the person to choose a format on the instruction and do not call generate.
The format's provider is signed in. If it is not, tell the person to sign in to it in Settings and do not call generate.

Every required input has a picture or video you can tell from the command, or the picture above for a video format declaring none. If one has none, say which input is missing and do not call generate.
The person has not said they do not want an image or a video.

content.name: collect_generation

content.description: Generate one image or one video under this Send's instruction, made as the format the instruction names: its type says image or video, and its provider, model, ratio and quality — or those of the variation the person chose beside Send — say what it is made with. Name no model and no option; the format decides them. Read the format with read_format first. Attach each input it takes in inputs, by name: the picture or video block the person marked with # for it, or the picture above the block when the command points at nothing. Write the words yourself, naming every attached input as @name where the words mean it (@start). A video format declaring no input takes the picture above the block as @start. It refuses, before anything is spent, an input the format does not declare, a block of the wrong kind, a required input not given and an attached input the words do not name. This is the one paid generation available per Send. It stages a pending image or video after the block and returns a job id; call collect_generation with that job and block until it completes. With no format on the instruction it refuses, and you tell the person to choose a format on the instruction.

content.description: What this Send's format is and how it is used, before you write the words a picture or video is made from. Free: nothing is spent. It answers the format's title, type, provider and model, the variation chosen beside Send, the format's own words — instructions for using it, which you follow — and each input it takes: its name (the @name the words must use), its kind (a start frame, an end frame, a reference image, video or audio), whether it is required, and what its words say it is for. Joined to its ends by source and target edges leaving this node, so staging one revises neither end. Proposed is the node being a candidate, not a state. Declared by ui.shell under BO_0244_006, anchored on claims until BO_0288_015 moved it to relations and gave it the block: any block says something, and a claim only ever existed where refinement had been.

A structure allows structures through offers, and a block may use a structure allowed by a structure on any block above it, never on itself. A structure says whether blocks may use it (blocks); the document always may. It carries fields, whose values a subject holds in a roleFields node. Retired, never deleted.

content.rationale: BO_0309 gives every instance the built-in roles Keyword, Profile, Format and Source (BO_0308_Q5), with the fixed ids builtin:keyword, builtin:profile, builtin:format and builtin:source and builtin: true. The route answers one script creating those the instance does not hold, and nothing when it holds them all, so a person's fields and offers on a built-in are never overwritten by a release. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0309 makes document roles and block roles one role type. A node never changes its type, so the route answers one script that makes each documentRole a new blockRole carrying its name, description and retired flag and its old id as formerId, placed after the roles already there; re-relates each offers from it and each document's hasDocumentRole to it as the new role's offers and the document's hasBlockRole, closing the old relations; and retires the old node. Nothing is lost: block roles keep their ids and their assignments, a reader holding a former id finds the role by it, and every document and block answers the same role names. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003), on this instance and on every install that takes the release.

BO_0310 makes Keyword offer the built-ins Definition and Alias on every instance, through offers a release makes, and sends the definition with a prompt. The built-ins themselves are created by migration-bo-0309-builtin-roles, which now holds them. The route answers one script relating the offers that do not stand, and setting sendWithPrompt to [builtin:definition] where Keyword holds none, so a person's switches are never reset by an upgrade; nothing when all stand. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0312 makes Format's release fields available on every instance: the required type choice and the schema text field. The migration preserves fields a person added and installs or repairs only the two release fields.

BO_0313 makes a source a document carrying the built-in Source, its CSL record the role's fields: Kind (a required choice of every CSL type), Authors and Editors (long text, one Family, Given per line), Issued, Container, Volume, Issue, Pages, Publisher, Place, DOI, ISBN, URL, Accessed (text), Abstract (long text), Tags (text), File (file) and Fetched (text). The route answers one SET of Source's fields that installs or repairs these release fields by key and keeps every field a person added beside them; an instance where they stand answers an empty statement.

BO_0336 moves what a picture or a video is made with into the format: Format's release fields gain provider, model, ratio and quality, open text fields suggesting from media's sources; Profile's gain format, an optional reference to a document carrying Format; Variation carries the same four; and Format offers Variation. The route answers one script relating the offer where it does not stand and installing or repairing those release fields by key, keeping every field a person added; nothing when all stand. Nothing migrates a profile's former type or backend: a profile names a format by the person's choice.

BO_0336 adds the built-in Variation (builtin:variation), a block's role offered by Format, naming another way to make a format. The route is builtin-roles', which answers one script creating the built-ins an instance does not hold, so it creates Variation with its release fields here and nothing where it stands. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

BO_0338_022: a built-in's name and description are the release's, and the release now names Profile Instruction. The route answers one script setting every built-in's stored name and description to the release's where they differ, the node and its id kept, nothing when all match. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

ME_0002_002: the built-in Input — a format's input, allowed by Format by the release — reaches an instance whose structures are documents already. Its document is made from the release under its fixed id where the instance holds none, with its release fields Kind, Name and Required as blocks using Field; Format allows it by the release, which the catalogue reads. The route answers nothing where Input stands, as on an instance that took structures-as-documents with it. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it.

RO_0005_002: a structure is a document. Every blockRole becomes a document using the built-in Structure: its name the title, its description the first block, each field a block using Field under the key it had, what it allowed and whether blocks may use it values of Structure, the ids it had kept; the built-ins are made from the release under their fixed ids where the instance holds none; every hasBlockRole to an old node is related again to its document and every roleFields for it names the document. The route answers one script, nothing once every structure is a document. It runs after this extension's own migrations that write structures as nodes; the extensions depending on structures run theirs after it. The kernel runs it once per instance when it serves the pin that carries it (BO_0312_003).

content.name: hasDocumentRole

content.name: offers
content.semantics: A structure allows a structure: directed from one blockRole to another, any number each way (BO_0309). A block may use a structure allowed by a structure on itself or on any block above it in its reading order, the document counting as the top. Declared by doc-block-structures under BO_0299_011, widened by BO_0309.

conventions.aStructureIsADocument: A structure is itself a document using Structure (read_document_structures says so of it): its title names it, its other blocks describe it, and each block using Field is one of its fields, its words the field's name and Field's values its type, whether it is required, its options and its default. To propose a structure, start a document for it and propose Structure on that document with propose_structures; to propose a field, propose a block in a structure's document and give it Field with its values. Structure is never proposed on a block, and a built-in's fields are the release's. It stands only once the person accepts it. A propose_structures that is refused, or whose staging is answered as refused, proposed nothing: tell the person what was refused and why, and never that the structure stands.
conventions.allowedFromAbove: A structure allows other structures: a block can use a structure that a structure used above it allows, at any depth, and a structure no structure allows on any block.
conventions.documentRolesOnTheDocument: A structure marked documentOnly — Keyword, Instruction, Format and Source always — is used by the document alone: propose it on the document, never on a block, and propose_structures refuses it on a block. A block's structure marked notOnBlock was used before the structure became the document's alone; leave it unless the person asks you to clear it. A part that should use a document structure on its own is a block's focused work, whose document uses it.
conventions.profileSaysHow: An instruction may say how a structure is written; its own blocks can use the same structures. Where the instruction speaks to a structure, follow it; where it is silent, the structure's description, its fields and its name are the guide.
conventions.proposeWhenAsked: Propose a structure or a value with propose_structures when the command asks for it, or when a value the command needs is missing and the words say what it is. A structure or a value the person set is rewritten only on the person's word. It stands only once the person accepts it.
conventions.readRolesFirst: Before proposing into a document, call read_document_structures once. The answer carries the structures the document uses and, per block in reading order, the structures it uses, each with its description, its fields and their values, what is missing, and which structures the block can use (usable).
conventions.roleIsNotTheTypographicRole: A block's structures are not its role in read_document: that one is the typographic role — paragraph, h1, quote.
conventions.roledBlockIsThePlace: When the command asks for what a structure is for and a block already uses that structure, propose a rewrite of that block or answer from it; never insert a second block of the structure. Insert one only where no block uses it; an empty block using a structure is asking to be written.
conventions.writeByRole: A block's structures say what the block is for: write a Hook as a hook, a Closing as a closing that answers the hook. The structure's description is the person's own account of it and outranks your idea of the word. A block using several structures serves each.

content.goal: Write a document by the structures its blocks use: each block by the structures the person gave it, the whole by the document's own; and, where the command asks for it, propose a structure or a value for the person to accept.
content.outputContract: A conclusion naming the structures you wrote under and which structures the proposed blocks serve, and any structure or value you proposed; the blocks and the proposed structures and values staged into the run's group.
content.permittedOperations: read_document_structures to read the structures and their values; propose_structures to propose using or clearing a structure, or a field's value; propose_document_changes to propose the words.
preconditions: read_document_structures answers for the document. If nothing in it uses a structure and the command asks for none, write it as you would any document and read nothing more here.
You can name the block you are writing into or proposing for; its structures are read by blockId from the answer.

content.description: Propose structures for one block, or for the document when you name no block: structures to use and to clear, and values for a structure's fields. It is staged into your proposals and stands only once the person accepts it. A structure must be one the block can use where it stands (read_document_structures' usable), and a value one of its field's type — a date as YYYY-MM-DD, a choice as one of its options.

block.description: The block, as a record id; leave it out for the document's own structures.

document.description: The document, as a record id.

values.description: Values by structure id, then by field key.

content.name: propose_structures

content.description: The structures the document uses and each block's, in reading order, at your pin: several per block, each with its description, its fields and their values, and the missing required ones; and per block the structures it can use where it stands (usable). What the person established, never a candidate's. Read it before proposing into a document whose blocks use structures, and write each block by its structures: a Hook block is written as a hook.

document.description: The document, as a record id.

content.name: read_document_structures
attachment

properties.file: a blob reference to the file's bytes; writing the node references them, so the blob store keeps them past the staging TTL
properties.filename: the file's name as the person attached it
properties.id: the attachment's identity, a UUID the shell mints when the command is sent; the node id is node:<id>
properties.mediaType: the file's media type: the browser's when it named one, else sniffed from its first bytes, else its extension's
properties.size: the file's size in bytes, at most 10 MB
properties.text: a blob reference to the text extracted from a PDF or Office document; absent for a file that is its own text and for any file with none
properties.textStatus: what a run can read of the file: text, extracted, empty (a PDF with no text layer or an Office file with no text), image, or none

content.semantics: The record of a file a person sent with a command: written as that person when the command is sent, one node per file, and named by the run it was sent with. It is the frame's, not a document's: nothing contains it and it contains nothing. Declared by ui.shell under BO_0229_007.
